title: Stream-slicer: KV-aware microbatcher with GPU slab throttling for low-jitter streaming completions
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Streaming chat completions show intermittent tail-jitter and occasional OOMs when high-concurrency sessions hold large KV caches. Current continuous batcher aggregates by arrival time and GPU free space but lacks fine-grained signaling about per-session KV pressure and upcoming token demand. This ticket proposes 'Stream-slicer', a microbatch formation heuristic that considers per-session token-rate forecasts, KV-slot pressure indicators, and GPU slab reservation signals to form low-jitter microbatches while preserving throughput and avoiding OOMs.
problem_statement: Users experience 95th+ token latency spikes during streaming completions under mixed workloads (bursting short chats + long context chats). Dedicated GPU memory pressure caused by large KV caches and slice-unfriendly batching increases tail latency and triggers reactive evictions that reduce quality. We need an adaptive batch formation policy that minimizes jitter for streaming while maintaining GPU utilization and KV cache health.
proposed_solution: Implement Stream-slicer: 1) Per-session slice metadata capturing recent token-rate, avg completion length, and kv-slot-growth; 2) A microbatch planner that prioritizes slicing short/high-interactivity sessions into small, frequent microbatches (low-latency path) while coalescing background tokens into larger batches; 3) GPU slab throttling: reserve a configurable memory slab per-GPU for live streaming sessions and enforce admission control when slab headroom < threshold; 4) KV-aware prefetch/eviction hints: mark slots as 'hot-probable' and proactively keep them in a small fast slab or prefetch on canary predictions; 5) Jitter-smoothing window to avoid oscillation in batch sizes across rapid arrival-rate changes.
acceptance_criteria: 95th token latency for streaming completions reduced by >= 20% on internal mixed workload benchmark compared to current baseline
No increase in GPU OOM incidents in canary cluster for 2 weeks of production-like load
End-to-end quality (greedy BLEU/ROUGE surrogate on eval prompts) shows <1% regression due to KV prefetch/eviction changes
Feature toggle exists to enable/disable Stream-slicer for canary/rollback
Dashboard panels added: per-GPU slab utilization, per-session slice size distribution, KV-slot hotness heatmap
implementation_plan: Design doc + sequence diagrams (Confluence): explain metadata flow between router, batcher, and runtime
Prototype microbatch planner in staging using local runtime flags (non-destructive) and synthetic workload
Add per-session slice metadata emission to request envelope and extend tracing headers
Implement GPU slab reservation checks in runtime admission path with configurable thresholds
Integrate KV-slot hotness tagging and a simple prefetch hint API consumed by runtime cache layer
Benchmark across Dedicated and Hosted dev clusters with mixed workloads (short-chat heavy, long-chat heavy, and bursty patterns)
Code review, security review if any KMS/KV metadata touches sensitive fields, and merge behind feature flag
Canary rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated SLO gates and rollback automation
tradeoffs: Increased scheduling complexity in batcher vs simpler time-based batching — more code surface to maintain
Reserving GPU slab reduces peak theoretical throughput slightly but improves tail-latency and reliability
KV prefetch increases memory churn and network I/O in some cases; must be conservative by default
More metadata in request envelope slightly increases request size and tracing complexity
testing: Unit tests for slice metadata lifecycle and admission logic
Integration tests with mock KV cache to validate hotness tagging and eviction hints
GPU stress tests reproducing tight-memory conditions to validate slab enforcement and graceful admission rejection
Perf bench harness runs comparing baseline vs Stream-slicer across 3 workloads (short-chat, long-chat, mixed) measuring p50/p95/p99 token latency and tokens/sec
Chaos test: simulate worker restarts mid-stream and validate session reconnection semantics and KV rehydration behavior
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal QA in dev cluster with feature flag enabled by runtime team only
Phase 1: Canary on Dedicated cluster (5% traffic) monitor SLOs for 72 hours
Phase 2: Broader canary (25%), run A/B traffic with control for quality evals for 1 week
Phase 3: Full rollout to Dedicated, then controlled rollout to Hosted tier with opt-in for customers initially
Rollback: immediate disable feature flag and rapid warmup of original batcher if metrics regress beyond thresholds
monitoring_and_alerting: New dashboard card: per-GPU streaming slab headroom (alert at < 10% for 5m)
Per-session jitter metric: 95th token latency per-session (alert if > baseline * 1.2)
KV OOM counter and eviction rate (alert on > 3x baseline over 15m)
Canary SLO gates automated for rollout orchestration
decisions: Keep client API unchanged — all batching heuristics are server-side only
Make KV prefetch opt-in and controlled by config flag tied to model family and customer tier
Default slab reservation per-GPU at 8% of device memory for streaming live sessions (configurable)
Use conservative prefetch budget (max 2 concurrent prefetch ops per worker) to limit network pressure
